![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

In environments with high disk I/O latency or slow CPU scheduling (such as CI virtual machines), the file replacement might briefly result in an `ENOENT` error during `statSync`, which adds `-1` to the `sizes` set as explicitly handled in the `catch` block. If `-1` is added, `partialStates` will contain `-1`, causing the assertion `expect(partialStates).toEqual([])` to fail flakily.

Since a missing file is not a partially written file, `-1` should be filtered out of `partialStates` to ensure the test remains robust and non-flaky.

```suggestion
    const partialStates = [...sizes].filter((size) => size !== SIZE && size !== -1);
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Relying on real-time measurements (`Date.now()`) in tests is highly prone to flakiness in CI environments (e.g., GitHub Actions), where CPU scheduling delays can easily cause a 10ms sleep to take more than 45ms.

Instead of asserting on elapsed time, we can robustly assert that `p2` rejected *before* `p1` completed by checking the state of the `events` array at that moment. Since `p1` takes 50ms to complete, at the time `p2` rejects, `p1` should still be running, meaning `events` should only contain `['p1:start']`.

```suggestion
    expect(events).toEqual(['p1:start']);
```
